column1: # kind|MM-DD|year|Greek name|English name|English biography   (English versions of the short biographies in data/bios; kind is always bio)

bio|04-21|1882|Πέρσι Γουίλλιαμς Μπρίντγκμαν|Percy Williams Bridgman|Percy Bridgman was an American physicist. He studied the behaviour of matter under very high pressures and in 1946 was awarded the Nobel Prize in Physics. He also developed the philosophy of "operationalism" in science.

bio|04-21|1910|Μαρκ Τουαίην|Mark Twain|Mark Twain, whose real name was Samuel Clemens, was an American writer. He wrote "The Adventures of Tom Sawyer" and "The Adventures of Huckleberry Finn", with humour and social criticism. He died in 1910.

bio|04-21|1915|Άντονι Κουίν|Anthony Quinn|Anthony Quinn was born in Mexico and grew up in the United States. He was an actor and played "Alexis Zorba" in the film by Michael Cacoyannis. He won two Academy Awards for Best Supporting Actor.

bio|04-21|1926|Βασίλισσα Ελισάβετ Β΄|Elizabeth II|Elizabeth II became Queen of the United Kingdom in 1952 and reigned for 70 years, the longest reign in British history. She was also head of the Commonwealth. She died in 2022 and was succeeded by her son Charles III.

bio|04-21|1946|Τζων Μέυναρντ Κέυνς|John Maynard Keynes|John Maynard Keynes was a British economist. In his work "The General Theory of Employment, Interest and Money" he argued that the state must intervene to deal with recession. He took part in the Bretton Woods conference.

bio|04-21|2016|Prince|Prince|Prince was an American singer, guitarist and producer. He became famous with the album and film "Purple Rain" and with songs such as "Kiss" and "When Doves Cry". He died in 2016.

bio|04-22|571|Μωάμεθ|Muhammad|Muhammad was born in Mecca and is the prophet and founder of Islam. According to tradition, he received revelations that formed the Quran. In 622 he moved to Medina, and by his death in 632 he had united much of Arabia.

bio|04-22|1616|Μιγκέλ ντε Θερβάντες|Miguel de Cervantes|Miguel de Cervantes was a Spanish writer. He wrote "Don Quixote", which is considered the first modern novel. He had fought in the naval battle of Lepanto and had been captured by pirates in Algeria.

bio|04-22|1724|Ιμμάνουελ Καντ|Immanuel Kant|Immanuel Kant was born in Königsberg and was a German philosopher. He wrote the "Critique of Pure Reason" and proposed the "categorical imperative" as the basis of ethics. He is considered one of the greatest philosophers of the West.

bio|04-22|1870|Βλαντίμιρ Λένιν|Vladimir Lenin|Vladimir Lenin, real name Ulyanov, was a Russian revolutionary and leader of the Bolsheviks. He led the October Revolution of 1917 and became head of the Soviet government. He died in 1924.

bio|04-22|1899|Βλαντίμιρ Ναμπόκοφ|Vladimir Nabokov|Vladimir Nabokov was a Russian writer who lived in Europe and in the United States. He wrote in Russian and in English and is best known for the novel "Lolita" and for "Pale Fire".

bio|04-22|1904|Ρόμπερτ Οπενχάιμερ|Robert Oppenheimer|Robert Oppenheimer was an American physicist and director of the Los Alamos laboratory in the Manhattan Project. He is regarded as the "father of the atomic bomb". After the war his loyalty was called into question.

bio|04-22|1937|Τζακ Νίκολσον|Jack Nicholson|Jack Nicholson is an American actor. He won three Oscars, for the films "One Flew Over the Cuckoo's Nest", "Terms of Endearment" and "As Good as It Gets", and he appeared in "The Shining".

bio|04-22|1986|Μίρτσεα Ελιάντε|Mircea Eliade|Mircea Eliade died in Chicago in 1986. He was a Romanian historian of religions and a writer, and he wrote "The Sacred and the Profane" as well as many literary works. He taught at the University of Chicago.

bio|04-22|1989|Εμίλιο Τζίνο Σεγκρέ|Emilio Gino Segrè|Emilio Segrè was an Italian physicist who lived in the United States. He discovered technetium and the antiproton, and in 1959 he shared the Nobel Prize in Physics with Owen Chamberlain.

bio|04-22|1994|Ρίτσαρντ Νίξον|Richard Nixon|Richard Nixon died in 1994. He was the 37th president of the United States and the only one to resign, in 1974, because of the Watergate scandal. He opened relations with China in 1972.

bio|04-23|1200|Τσου Σι|Zhu Xi|Zhu Xi was a Chinese philosopher and scholar of the Song dynasty. He developed Neo-Confucianism and classified the Confucian texts, which became the basis of education in China for centuries.

bio|04-23|1564|Ουίλιαμ Σαίξπηρ|William Shakespeare|William Shakespeare was born in Stratford-upon-Avon. He was an English playwright and poet. He wrote 37 plays, such as "Hamlet", "Othello", "King Lear" and "Romeo and Juliet". His date of birth is traditional, as only his baptism is known.

bio|04-23|1605|Μπορίς Γκοντουνόφ|Boris Godunov|Boris Godunov was tsar of Russia from 1598 to 1605. He was a powerful official and gained the throne when Feodor I died without an heir. His reign was marked by famine and uprisings.

bio|04-23|1791|Τζέιμς Μπιουκάναν|James Buchanan|James Buchanan was the 15th president of the United States, from 1857 to 1861. He failed to prevent the crisis that led to the American Civil War, and his presidency is often judged negatively.

bio|04-23|1858|Μαξ Πλανκ|Max Planck|Max Planck was a German physicist. In 1900 he introduced the concept of the energy quantum to explain black-body radiation and became the founder of quantum theory. In 1918 he was awarded the Nobel Prize in Physics.

bio|04-23|1891|Σεργκέι Προκόφιεφ|Sergei Prokofiev|Sergei Prokofiev was a Russian composer and pianist. He wrote "Peter and the Wolf", the ballet "Romeo and Juliet" and the "Classical Symphony". He lived abroad for many years and later returned to the Soviet Union.

bio|04-23|1902|Χαλντόρ Λάξνες|Halldór Laxness|Halldór Laxness was an Icelandic writer. He wrote novels about life in the countryside of Iceland, such as "Independent People". In 1955 he was awarded the Nobel Prize in Literature.

bio|04-23|1928|Σίρλεϊ Τεμπλ|Shirley Temple|Shirley Temple was an American actress who became a worldwide star as a child in the 1930s. She played in films such as "Heidi" and "Little Miss Marker". Later she became a diplomat and served as United States ambassador.

bio|04-23|2007|Μπορίς Γιέλτσιν|Boris Yeltsin|Boris Yeltsin died in 2007. He was the first president of the Russian Federation, from 1991 to 1999, and he confronted the coup of 1991 and the dissolution of the Soviet Union.

bio|04-23|2013|Μοχάμεντ Ομάρ|Mohammed Omar|Mullah Mohammed Omar was the founder and leader of the Taliban in Afghanistan. He governed the country from 1996 to 2001, when the United States overthrew the regime. His death became known in 2015.

bio|04-24|1731|Ντάνιελ Ντεφόε|Daniel Defoe|Daniel Defoe was an English writer and journalist. He wrote the novel "Robinson Crusoe" in 1719, which is considered one of the first English novels. He also wrote "Moll Flanders".

bio|04-24|1815|Άντονι Τρόλοπ|Anthony Trollope|Anthony Trollope was an English writer of the Victorian era. He wrote series of novels, such as the "Barchester Chronicles" and the "Palliser" novels, with observations on society and politics. He also worked for the post office.
bio|04-24|1845|Καρλ Σπίτελερ|Carl Spitteler|Carl Spitteler was a Swiss poet. He wrote the epic "Olympian Spring" and in 1919 was awarded the Nobel Prize in Literature.

bio|04-24|1856|Φιλίπ Πεταίν|Philippe Pétain|Philippe Pétain was a French marshal and a hero of the Battle of Verdun in the First World War. In 1940 he became head of the Vichy government, which collaborated with Nazi Germany, and after the war he was sentenced.

bio|04-24|1891|Χέλμουτ Καρλ φον Μόλτκε|Helmuth von Moltke|Helmuth von Moltke was a Prussian field marshal. He was chief of the general staff and organised Prussia's victories over Austria in 1866 and over France in 1870-1871. He is regarded as one of the most important strategists of the 19th century.

bio|04-24|1934|Σίρλεϊ Μακ Λέιν|Shirley MacLaine|Shirley MacLaine is an American actress and writer. She won the Academy Award for Best Supporting Actress for the film "Terms of Endearment" and appeared in "The Apartment" and "Irma la Douce".

bio|04-24|1942|Μπάρμπρα Στράιζαντ|Barbra Streisand|Barbra Streisand is an American singer, actress and director. She won an Oscar for the film "Funny Girl" and sold hundreds of millions of records. She has won Oscars, Emmys, Grammys and Tonys.

bio|04-24|1960|Μαξ φον Λάουε|Max von Laue|Max von Laue was a German physicist. He discovered the diffraction of X-rays by crystals and in 1914 was awarded the Nobel Prize in Physics. He opposed the Nazis and helped colleagues who were persecuted.
bio|04-24|1980|Αλέχο Καρπεντιέ|Alejo Carpentier|Alejo Carpentier was a Cuban writer and musicologist. He wrote the novel "The Kingdom of This World" and developed the concept of "magical realism".

bio|04-25|1472|Λέον Μπαττίστα Αλμπέρτι|Leon Battista Alberti|Leon Battista Alberti was an Italian architect, art theorist and humanist of the Renaissance. He wrote the works "On Painting" and "On Architecture" and designed buildings in Florence and Mantua.

bio|04-25|1595|Τορκουάτο Τάσσο|Torquato Tasso|Torquato Tasso was an Italian poet of the Renaissance. He wrote the epic "Jerusalem Delivered". He died in Rome in 1595, shortly before he was to be crowned as a poet on the Capitol.

bio|04-25|1599|Όλιβερ Κρόμγουελ|Oliver Cromwell|Oliver Cromwell was an English soldier and politician. He led the army of Parliament in the English Civil War and contributed to the execution of Charles I. From 1653 to 1658 he was Lord Protector of England.
bio|04-25|1744|Άντερς Κέλσιος|Anders Celsius|Anders Celsius was a Swedish astronomer. In 1742 he proposed the temperature scale that bears his name. He was a professor of astronomy at Uppsala.

bio|04-25|1874|Γουλιέλμο Μαρκόνι|Guglielmo Marconi|Guglielmo Marconi was an Italian inventor and businessman. He developed wireless telegraphy and in 1901 sent the first signal across the Atlantic. In 1909 he shared the Nobel Prize in Physics.

bio|04-25|1900|Βόλφγκανγκ Πάουλι|Wolfgang Pauli|Wolfgang Pauli was an Austrian physicist. He formulated the Pauli exclusion principle and predicted the neutrino. In 1945 he was awarded the Nobel Prize in Physics.

bio|04-25|1940|Αλ Πατσίνο|Al Pacino|Al Pacino is an American actor. He became famous for the role of Michael Corleone in "The Godfather" and won the Academy Award for Best Actor for "Scent of a Woman". He also appeared in "Scarface".

bio|04-25|1947|Γιόχαν Κρόιφ|Johan Cruyff|Johan Cruyff was born in Amsterdam and was a Dutch footballer and coach. He was the leading figure of "total football" at Ajax and in the Netherlands, and he won the Ballon d'Or three times.

bio|04-25|1995|Τζίντζερ Ρότζερς|Ginger Rogers|Ginger Rogers was an American actress and dancer. She became famous for the musicals she made with Fred Astaire, such as "Top Hat". She won the Academy Award for Best Actress for "Kitty Foyle".

bio|04-26|121|Μάρκος Αυρήλιος|Marcus Aurelius|Marcus Aurelius was a Roman emperor from 161 to 180 and a Stoic philosopher. He wrote his personal reflections in Greek, known as the "Meditations". He was the last of the "Five Good Emperors".

bio|04-26|1798|Ευγένιος Ντελακρουά|Eugène Delacroix|Eugène Delacroix was a French painter of the Romantic movement. He painted "Liberty Leading the People" and "The Massacre at Chios", a work that stirred Europe's feelings about the Greek War of Independence.

bio|04-26|1889|Λούντβιχ Βίτγκενσταϊν|Ludwig Wittgenstein|Ludwig Wittgenstein was born in Vienna and was a philosopher. He wrote the "Tractatus Logico-Philosophicus" and the "Philosophical Investigations". He is considered one of the most important philosophers of the 20th century.

bio|04-26|1910|Μπιέρνστιερνε Μπιέρνσον|Bjørnstjerne Bjørnson|Bjørnstjerne Bjørnson was a Norwegian writer and politician. He wrote the short story "Synnøve Solbakken" and the lyrics of Norway's national anthem. In 1903 he was awarded the Nobel Prize in Literature.

bio|04-26|1917|Ι.Μ. Πέι|I. M. Pei|I. M. Pei was a Chinese-American architect. He designed the Louvre Pyramid and the Rock and Roll Hall of Fame Museum. In 1983 he was awarded the Pritzker Prize, and he died in 2019.

bio|04-26|1920|Σρινιβάσα Ραμανούτζαν|Srinivasa Ramanujan|Srinivasa Ramanujan was an Indian mathematician. He was self-taught and discovered thousands of formulas in number theory and series, and he collaborated with Hardy at Cambridge. He died young, at the age of 32.

bio|04-26|1951|Άρνολντ Σόμμερφελντ|Arnold Sommerfeld|Arnold Sommerfeld was a German physicist. He extended Bohr's atomic model and was the teacher of many well-known physicists, such as Heisenberg, Pauli and Bethe.
bio|04-26|1963|Τζετ Λι|Jet Li|Jet Li was born in China and is a martial artist and actor. He starred in films such as "Once Upon a Time in China" and "Lethal Weapon 4". He was a Wushu champion.

bio|04-26|1989|Λουσίλ Μπολ|Lucille Ball|Lucille Ball was an American comedian. She starred in the television series "I Love Lucy", one of the most successful series in American television. She also became a producer.

bio|04-27|1521|Φερδινάνδος Μαγγελάνος|Ferdinand Magellan|Ferdinand Magellan was a Portuguese explorer in the service of Spain. He led the first expedition that attempted to circumnavigate the Earth, in 1519. He was killed in 1521 in the Philippines, and Elcano completed the voyage.

bio|04-27|1759|Μαίρη Γουόλστονκραφτ|Mary Wollstonecraft|Mary Wollstonecraft was an English writer and philosopher. In her book "A Vindication of the Rights of Woman" of 1792 she argued for the education and equality of women. She was the mother of Mary Shelley.

bio|04-27|1791|Σάμουελ Μορς|Samuel Morse|Samuel Morse was born in Massachusetts. He was a painter and inventor, and he developed the electric telegraph and the Morse code. In 1844 he sent the first message from Washington to Baltimore.

bio|04-27|1820|Χέρμπερτ Σπένσερ|Herbert Spencer|Herbert Spencer was an English philosopher and sociologist. He applied the idea of evolution to societies and introduced the phrase "survival of the fittest".

bio|04-27|1822|Οδυσσεύς Γκραντ|Ulysses S. Grant|Ulysses S. Grant was a Union general in the American Civil War and the 18th president of the United States, from 1869 to 1877. He accepted the surrender of Lee at Appomattox in 1865. His presidency was marked by corruption scandals.

bio|04-27|1937|Αντόνιο Γκράμσι|Antonio Gramsci|Antonio Gramsci died in 1937, a few days after his release from prison. He was an Italian philosopher and leader of the Communist Party, who was imprisoned by Mussolini and wrote the "Prison Notebooks".

bio|04-27|1938|Έντμουντ Χούσερλ|Edmund Husserl|Edmund Husserl died in Freiburg in 1938. He was a German philosopher and the founder of phenomenology, which had a major influence on Heidegger and Sartre.

bio|04-27|1967|Γουλιέλμος Αλέξανδρος|Willem-Alexander|Willem-Alexander has been king of the Netherlands since 2013, when his mother Beatrix resigned. He is the first male king of the country since 1890. He is married to Máxima.

bio|04-27|1972|Κβάμε Νκρούμαχ|Kwame Nkrumah|Kwame Nkrumah was a Ghanaian politician. He led the struggle for Ghana's independence from Britain and became the country's first prime minister and then its president. He was a supporter of Pan-Africanism and was overthrown in 1966.

bio|04-28|1758|Τζέιμς Μονρόε|James Monroe|James Monroe was the 5th president of the United States, from 1817 to 1825. In 1823 he set out the "Monroe Doctrine", which warned European powers not to intervene in the American continent. He also supported the Greek Revolution.

bio|04-28|1813|Μιχαήλ Κουτούζοφ|Mikhail Kutuzov|Mikhail Kutuzov was a Russian field marshal. He led the Russian army in the war of 1812 against Napoleon and left Moscow in order to save the army. He died in 1813.

bio|04-28|1906|Κουρτ Γκέντελ|Kurt Gödel|Kurt Gödel was born in Moravia and was a logician and mathematician. He proved the incompleteness theorems in 1931. He lived at Princeton and was a friend of Einstein.

bio|04-28|1918|Γκαβρίλο Πρίντσιπ|Gavrilo Princip|Gavrilo Princip was a Serb from Bosnia and a member of the "Young Bosnia" movement. On 28 June 1914 he assassinated Archduke Franz Ferdinand in Sarajevo, an event that led to the First World War. He died in prison in 1918.

bio|04-28|1937|Σαντάμ Χουσεΐν|Saddam Hussein|Saddam Hussein was president of Iraq from 1979 to 2003. His war with Iran and the invasion of Kuwait in 1990 led to major conflicts. He was overthrown by the invasion of 2003 and was executed in 2006.

bio|04-28|1945|Μπενίτο Μουσολίνι|Benito Mussolini|Benito Mussolini was the founder of Italian fascism and dictator of Italy from 1922. He allied himself with Hitler, and he was arrested and executed by Italian partisans on 28 April 1945.

bio|04-28|1945|Κλαρέττα Πετάτσι|Clara Petacci|Clara Petacci was the mistress of Benito Mussolini. She was arrested together with him and was executed by partisans on 28 April 1945, while they were trying to escape to Switzerland.

bio|04-28|1974|Πενέλοπε Κρουζ|Penélope Cruz|Penélope Cruz is a Spanish actress. She won the Academy Award for Best Supporting Actress for the film "Vicky Cristina Barcelona" and has appeared in films by Pedro Almodóvar, such as "All About My Mother".

bio|04-28|1981|Τζέσικα Άλμπα|Jessica Alba|Jessica Alba is an American actress and businesswoman. She became known through the series "Dark Angel" and the films "Sin City" and "Fantastic Four". She founded the company Honest Company.

bio|04-29|1854|Ανρί Πουανκαρέ|Henri Poincaré|Henri Poincaré was a French mathematician and physicist. He contributed to the theory of dynamical systems and to topology, with the Poincaré conjecture, and to the foundations of the theory of relativity.

bio|04-29|1901|Χιροχίτο|Hirohito|Hirohito was emperor of Japan from 1926 to 1989. The country fought in the Second World War, and in 1945 he announced the surrender. After the war he became the symbolic head of state.

bio|04-29|1951|Λούντβιχ Βίτγκενσταϊν|Ludwig Wittgenstein|Ludwig Wittgenstein died in Cambridge in 1951 from cancer. He was an Austrian philosopher who wrote the "Tractatus" and the "Philosophical Investigations", and he deeply influenced the philosophy of language.

bio|04-29|1968|Κολίντα Γκράμπαρ-Κιτάροβιτς|Kolinda Grabar-Kitarović|Kolinda Grabar-Kitarović is a Croatian politician. She was the first woman president of Croatia, from 2015 to 2020, and she had served as foreign minister and as an assistant secretary general of NATO.

bio|04-29|1974|Anggun|Anggun|Anggun is an Indonesian singer. She moved to France and built an international career, with songs in English and in French. She has been honoured by France as a Knight of the Legion of Honour.

bio|04-29|1980|Άλφρεντ Χίτσκοκ|Alfred Hitchcock|Alfred Hitchcock was an English director, known as "the master of suspense". He directed the films "Psycho", "The Birds", "Rear Window" and "Vertigo". He died in 1980.
bio|04-29|2008|Άλμπερτ Χόφμαν|Albert Hofmann|Albert Hofmann was a Swiss chemist. In 1938 he synthesised LSD and in 1943 he discovered its psychoactive properties. He died in 2008 at the age of 102.
bio|04-29|2014|Μπομπ Χόσκινς|Bob Hoskins|Bob Hoskins was an English actor. He became known for the films "Mona Lisa" and "Who Framed Roger Rabbit", and he also appeared in "Hook" and "Nixon".

bio|04-30|453|Αττίλας|Attila|Attila was king of the Huns from 434 to 453. He attacked the Roman Empire and France, where he was defeated at the Battle of the Catalaunian Plains in 451. He died in 453, on the night of his wedding.

bio|04-30|1777|Καρλ Φρίντριχ Γκάους|Carl Friedrich Gauss|Carl Friedrich Gauss was born in Braunschweig and was a German mathematician and physicist. He contributed to number theory, geometry, statistics and magnetism. He is called the "Prince of Mathematicians".
bio|04-30|1883|Γιάροσλαβ Χάσεκ|Jaroslav Hašek|Jaroslav Hašek was a Czech writer. He wrote the satirical novel "The Adventures of the Good Soldier Švejk". He died in 1923.
bio|04-30|1883|Εντουάρ Μανέ|Édouard Manet|Édouard Manet was a French painter and a forerunner of Impressionism. He painted "Luncheon on the Grass" and "Olympia". He died in Paris in 1883.

bio|04-30|1945|Αδόλφος Χίτλερ|Adolf Hitler|Adolf Hitler killed himself on 30 April 1945 in the Berlin bunker, as the Red Army approached. He was the dictator of Nazi Germany and was responsible for the Second World War and the Holocaust.
bio|04-30|1945|Εύα Μπράουν|Eva Braun|Eva Braun killed herself on 30 April 1945 in the Berlin bunker, together with Adolf Hitler, whom she had married one day earlier.

bio|04-30|1946|Κάρολος ΙΣΤ' Γουσταύος|Carl XVI Gustaf|Carl XVI Gustaf has been king of Sweden since 1973, when his grandfather Gustaf VI Adolf died. He married Silvia Sommerlath and has three children, with Victoria as his heir.
bio|04-30|1959|Στήβεν Χάρπερ|Stephen Harper|Stephen Harper is a Canadian politician of the Conservative Party. He was prime minister of Canada from 2006 to 2015.

bio|04-30|1982|Κίρστεν Ντανστ|Kirsten Dunst|Kirsten Dunst is an American actress. She became known as a child in the film "Interview with the Vampire" and later appeared in "Spider-Man" and "Melancholia".
bio|05-01|1245|Φίλιππος Γ΄|Philip III|Philip III the Bold was king of France from 1270 to 1285. He succeeded his father Louis IX during the crusade to Tunis and died on a campaign in Aragon.

bio|05-01|1672|Τζόζεφ Άντισον|Joseph Addison|Joseph Addison was an English writer and politician. Together with Richard Steele he published the periodicals "The Tatler" and "The Spectator", with essays on social life, and he wrote the tragedy "Cato".

bio|05-01|1852|Σαντιάγο Ραμόν ι Καχάλ|Santiago Ramón y Cajal|Santiago Ramón y Cajal was a Spanish doctor and neuroscientist. He studied the structure of the nervous system and argued that it is made up of independent cells, the neurons. In 1906 he shared the Nobel Prize with Golgi.

bio|05-01|1873|Ντέιβιντ Λίβινγκστον|David Livingstone|David Livingstone died in 1873 in Zambia while searching for the sources of the Nile. He was a Scottish missionary and explorer of Africa. His local assistants carried his body to the coast.

bio|05-01|1904|Αντονίν Ντβόρζακ|Antonín Dvořák|Antonín Dvořák was a Czech composer. He wrote the "From the New World" Symphony, the "Slavonic Dances" and a cello concerto. He lived for a time in the United States and died in Prague.
bio|05-01|1923|Τζόζεφ Χέλερ|Joseph Heller|Joseph Heller was an American writer. He wrote the novel "Catch-22", a satire of war set in the Second World War, which became famous in the 1960s.

bio|05-01|1945|Γιόζεφ Γκαίμπελς|Joseph Goebbels|Joseph Goebbels was the minister of propaganda of Nazi Germany. He was a passionate supporter of Hitler. He killed himself on 1 May 1945 in Berlin, together with his wife Magda, after they had killed their six children.

bio|05-01|1969|Γουές Άντερσον|Wes Anderson|Wes Anderson is an American director and screenwriter. He has a distinctive visual style and directed the films "The Royal Tenenbaums", "The Grand Budapest Hotel" and "Isle of Dogs".

bio|05-01|1994|Άιρτον Σένα|Ayrton Senna|Ayrton Senna was killed on 1 May 1994 in an accident at the Imola Grand Prix. He was a Brazilian Formula One driver who had won three world championships with McLaren.

bio|05-02|1519|Λεονάρντο ντα Βίντσι|Leonardo da Vinci|Leonardo da Vinci died at Clos Lucé, near Amboise in France, in 1519. He was a painter, inventor and scientist of the Renaissance, and he had painted the "Mona Lisa" and "The Last Supper".

bio|05-02|1729|Αικατερίνη Β΄ η Μεγάλη|Catherine the Great|Catherine the Great was empress of Russia from 1762 to 1796. She was born in Germany and took power in a coup. She expanded Russia towards the Black Sea and supported the arts and sciences.
bio|05-02|1772|Νοβάλις|Novalis|Novalis, real name Georg von Hardenberg, was a German poet of early Romanticism. He wrote the "Hymns to the Night". He died young, in 1801.

bio|05-02|1903|Μπινγκ Κρόσμπι|Bing Crosby|Bing Crosby was an American singer and actor. He was one of the great stars of the 1930s and 1940s and sang "White Christmas". He won an Oscar for the film "Going My Way".

bio|05-02|1945|Μάρτιν Μπόρμαν|Martin Bormann|Martin Bormann was head of the chancellery of the Nazi Party and Hitler's secretary. He was presumed to have died in Berlin in early May 1945. His remains were identified in the 1990s.

bio|05-02|1972|Ντουέιν Τζόνσον|Dwayne Johnson|Dwayne Johnson, known as "The Rock", is an American former wrestler and actor. He became famous in WWE and played in films such as "Fast & Furious" and "Moana".

bio|05-02|1975|Ντέιβιντ Μπέκαμ|David Beckham|David Beckham is an English former footballer. He played for Manchester United, Real Madrid and the England national team. He was known for taking free kicks, and he married Victoria Adams.

bio|05-02|2011|Οσάμα μπιν Λάντεν|Osama bin Laden|Osama bin Laden was killed on 2 May 2011 by United States special forces in Abbottabad, Pakistan. He was the founder of al-Qaeda and the mastermind of the attacks of 11 September 2001.

bio|05-03|1469|Νικολό Μακιαβέλι|Niccolò Machiavelli|Niccolò Machiavelli was an Italian politician and thinker from Florence. He wrote "The Prince", a work on the exercise of power with realism, and he is considered the founder of modern political theory.

bio|05-03|1481|Μωάμεθ Β΄ ο Πορθητής|Mehmed II the Conqueror|Mehmed II died in 1481. He was the Ottoman sultan who conquered Constantinople in 1453 and made the city the capital of his empire. He also conquered the Morea and Trebizond.

bio|05-03|1616|Ουίλλιαμ Σαίξπηρ|William Shakespeare|William Shakespeare died in 1616 in Stratford-upon-Avon, according to the old calendar. He was the greatest English playwright and wrote tragedies, comedies and historical plays.

bio|05-03|1892|Τζορτζ Τόμσον|George Paget Thomson|George Paget Thomson was an English physicist and the son of J. J. Thomson. He showed that electrons have wave properties and in 1937 shared the Nobel Prize in Physics.
